en.heading: 28 October: Korea's Corrections Day has a separate legal restoration
en.origin: Corrections Day acknowledges employees working in prisons and rehabilitation services and the importance of reintegration. Its anniversary recalls 28 October 1945, when correctional facilities were taken over from Japanese colonial administration. The government created a Corrections Officers Day on 28 October 1959, then merged it into Law Day on 30 March 1973. For decades it was not a distinct statutory commemoration. On 19 June 2002, Corrections Day regained separate statutory status. This is different from Law Day on 25 April, even though the two commemorations once shared an administrative history. When presenting the origin, distinguish the original event, the first dedicated activities and the later legal framework. A commemorative day must not be assumed to create a general national holiday.
en.promoter: South Korean government departments established the successive regulations that now govern this national commemoration, after earlier documented historical events.
en.purpose: Recognize the work of corrections personnel and support responsible rehabilitation and reintegration.

it.heading: 28 ottobre: la Giornata penitenziaria coreana torna autonoma
it.origin: La Giornata degli operatori penitenziari riconosce il lavoro nelle carceri e nei servizi di reinserimento. La data ricorda il 28 ottobre 1945, quando le strutture furono rilevate dall'amministrazione coloniale giapponese. Il governo istituì una Giornata degli agenti penitenziari il 28 ottobre 1959, poi la accorpò alla Giornata della legge il 30 marzo 1973. Per anni non fu una ricorrenza distinta. Il 19 giugno 2002 ottenne nuovamente un riconoscimento legale autonomo. Non coincide con la Giornata della legge del 25 aprile, pur avendo condiviso parte della storia amministrativa. Per raccontarne l'origine occorre distinguere evento iniziale, prime attività e quadro legislativo successivo. Una commemorazione non rende automaticamente festiva la giornata per tutti.
it.promoter: I ministeri del governo sudcoreano hanno stabilito le successive norme di questa ricorrenza dopo gli antecedenti storici documentati.
it.purpose: Riconoscere il lavoro degli operatori e sostenere il reinserimento e la riabilitazione delle persone detenute.

El Gobierno estableció un Día de los Funcionarios Penitenciarios en 1959, pero lo fusionó con el Día de la Ley el 30 de marzo de 1973. Durante años careció de reconocimiento separado. fr.heading: 28 octobre : la Journée pénitentiaire retrouve son statut autonome
fr.origin: La Journée des services pénitentiaires met en valeur le travail dans les prisons et les dispositifs de réinsertion. Elle rappelle le 28 octobre 1945, date du transfert des établissements hors de l'administration coloniale japonaise. Le gouvernement a créé une Journée des agents pénitentiaires en 1959, puis l'a intégrée à la Journée du droit le 30 mars 1973. La commémoration a donc perdu son statut séparé. Le 19 juin 2002, elle a retrouvé une reconnaissance légale autonome. Elle ne doit pas être confondue avec la Journée du droit du 25 avril malgré leur histoire partagée. Pour retracer son origine, il faut séparer l'événement initial, les premières activités et le droit ultérieur. Une journée commémorative n'est pas automatiquement fériée.

de.heading: 28. Oktober: Koreas Tag des Justizvollzugs wird wieder eigenständig

Oktober 1945, als Gefängniseinrichtungen aus der japanischen Kolonialverwaltung übernommen wurden. 1959 führte die Regierung einen eigenen Tag der Vollzugsbeamten ein, der am 30. März 1973 im Tag des Rechts aufging. Die eigenständige Anerkennung ging dadurch verloren. Am 19. Juni 2002 wurde der Tag erneut als gesetzlicher Anlass eingeführt. de.purpose: Die Arbeit des Vollzugspersonals und eine verantwortungsvolle Resozialisierung hervorheben.

en.heading: 22 April: from postal services to Information and Communications Day
en.origin: Information and Communications Day developed from Korea's postal-service history. In 1956, authorities created a Postal and Telecommunications Day associated with an 1884 ceremony celebrating the first Korean postal administration. On 7 July 1972 the date changed to 22 April, recalling the royal instruction to open the postal bureau in 1884. In 1973 postal carriers' commemorations were incorporated into the official day. On 30 May 1996 the government renamed it Information and Communications Day, extending the theme beyond traditional post. The 1884 event is a historical reference, not the modern statutory introduction date. When presenting the origin, distinguish the original event, the first dedicated activities and the later legal framework. A commemorative day must not be assumed to create a general national holiday.
en.promoter: South Korean government departments established the successive regulations that now govern this national commemoration, after earlier documented historical events.
en.purpose: Recognize communication services, digital infrastructure and the labour of people working in the sector.

en.heading: 31 May: Korea's Oceans Day and its maritime heritage
en.origin: Oceans Day in South Korea draws attention to the sea, marine livelihoods and maritime industries. The government's explanation also recalls the historic naval base at Cheonghaejin established by Jang Bogo during the Silla period. The Ministry of the Interior notes that May was chosen partly because it suited fishing communities and seasonal sea-related festivals. These customs preceded the modern commemorative law. The state designated 31 May as a statutory commemorative day on 30 May 1996. The historic maritime tradition and the government day have different timescales and should not be conflated. en.heading: 21 October: Korean Police Day and the post-liberation institution
en.origin: Police Day marks the establishment of South Korea's post-liberation policing institutions, with the original reference date of 21 October 1945 under the United States Military Government. The anniversary was recognized as National Police Foundation Day in 1948. The Ministry of the Interior issued a directive designating 21 October Police Day on 7 November 1957. A further institutional rule followed in 1971 and the day became a statutory commemoration on 30 March 1973. The 1945 organizational event, 1957 designation and 1973 legal status are separate milestones. When presenting the origin, distinguish the original event, the first dedicated activities and the later legal framework. A commemorative day must not be assumed to create a general national holiday.

en.heading: 1 October: the Korean Armed Forces Day unites military commemorations
en.origin: Armed Forces Day in South Korea recognizes the country's military personnel and their service. The chosen date refers to 1 October 1950, when South Korean forces crossed the 38th parallel during the Korean War. Separate branch-level anniversaries were held before the government consolidated the observance through a presidential regulation dated 21 September 1956, creating Armed Forces Day on 1 October. In 1973 it entered the national statutory commemorations framework. Its classification as a general public holiday has changed over time and must be checked separately for each calendar year. When presenting the origin, distinguish the original event, the first dedicated activities and the later legal framework. A commemorative day must not be assumed to create a general national holiday.
